items.title: 24.3.2 Distinction between Primary and Secondary Amines

source_refs.note: Topic 24.3.2 with Quick Check 24.3, as printed (PDF 123-124); the schemes are redrawn. Quick Check (d) prints the fish amine as 'N,N-dimethylammine' (marked).

blocks.text: Primary, secondary and tertiary aliphatic amines are identified and distinguished by reacting them with nitric (III) acid (nitrous acid). Primary amines react with nitrous acid to form diazonium salts. The process is called diazotization.

blocks.alt: NaNO2 + HCl gives HNO2 + NaCl. Below: CH3-CH2-NH2 (ethanamine) + HNO2 + HCl gives CH3-CH2-N(+) triple bond N Cl- (ethane diazonium chloride) + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Ethanamine and nitrous acid give ethane diazonium chloride (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 123).

blocks.text: Secondary amines form N-nitrosoamines (yellow oily liquid) on reaction with nitrous acid.

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-NH with CH3 on the N (N-methylethanamine) + HNO2, with NaNO2 + HCl over the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-N(CH3)-NO (N-methyl-N-nitrosoethanamine) + H2O.
blocks.caption: N-methylethanamine and nitrous acid give an N-nitrosoamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 124).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed equation reads ‘NH – HNO₂’; it is + HNO₂, as drawn above. The label printed ‘ethaneamine’ under the equation for primary amines is ethanamine.
Tertiary amines react with nitrous acid to form soluble salt.

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-N with two CH3 groups (N,N-dimethylethanamine) + HNO2 gives, in square brackets with a + charge, CH3-CH2-N(CH3)2-H, followed by NO2- (N,N-dimethylethanammonium nitrite, soluble).
blocks.caption: N,N-dimethylethanamine and nitrous acid give a soluble nitrite salt (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 124).

blocks.text: The summary of the above reaction is

items: Primary amines react with nitrous acid to produce nitrogen gas (seen as bubbles).
Secondary amines react with nitrous acid to produce yellow oily liquid.

blocks.text: Tertiary amines react with nitrous acid to form soluble nitrite salts. There is no visible sign of reaction.

blocks.title: Quick Check 24.3
blocks.text:
a) Phenylamine is about a million times less basic than cyclohexylamine. Give reason. (phenylamine Kb = 4.2 × 10⁻¹⁰; cyclohexylamine Kb = 3.3 × 10⁻⁴)
b) Which of ethanamine and propan-2-amine is more basic? Explain.
c) Show the reaction of propan-2-amine with HCl. Name the salt formed.
d) Which acid reacts with N,N-dimethylammine in fish when it is treated with vinegar? Write a chemical equation to show this reaction.

blocks.alt: Two structures side by side. Left: a benzene ring (hexagon with a circle inside) with NH2 on the top corner, labelled phenylamine, Kb = 4.2 × 10⁻¹⁰. Right: a plain hexagon (cyclohexane ring) with NH2 on the top corner, labelled cyclohexylamine, Kb = 3.3 × 10⁻⁴.
blocks.caption: Phenylamine and cyclohexylamine with their Kb values, Quick Check 24.3 (original drawing after the textbook's structures).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The amine in fish is N,N-dimethylmethanamine (trimethylamine), (CH₃)₃N, as the Did You Know box in 24.3.1 says; ‘N,N-dimethylammine’ is not a correct name.
